subject: rateyourbuild
note: prompters leaderboard rows carried both "board-row" and "user-chip" classes, and the two set conflicting display values (flex vs. inline-flex) with equal CSS specificity — the later one won, so rows flowed inline and multiple prompters could crowd onto one visual line instead of stacking one per row.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: featured review / featured community score picked list[hash(day) % list.length], so every new rating or review anywhere on the site (via the live subscription) changed the list length and reshuffled the pick — now hashes each candidate's own id against the day and takes the max, so the pick only changes if a new candidate genuinely wins, not on every unrelated new entry.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: every reply's rkey was `${subject}.${target}` — one overwrite-in-place slot per (replier, target) — so a second reply to the same person silently replaced the first instead of adding to the thread; a real back-and-forth could never accumulate past one message each side. Replies now get a unique rkey plus an explicit parentKey pointing at the exact comment they answer, so replying again always adds a new comment.

subject: nounlab
note: the countability card's count-noun example concatenated "another" with an indefinite article, rendering "We must build another a website!" — dropped the redundant article so it now reads "We must build another website!".

subject: rateyourbuild
note: 🔔 alerts only ever fired for a genuinely live Jetstream commit while the tab was open, so a rating/review or reply that landed while you weren't watching silently never alerted you, even though the site's own history backfill had it. Alerts now also catch up from that backfilled history against each subscription's own createdAt the next time you open the tab, deduped against anything already fired live.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: consolidated record — "I still see none from you" took three separate real bugs, each logged as its own entry last round, to actually resolve: the in-thread bot reply was gated on the "bugged" box (none of rateyourbuild's own reviews had it checked) and only kept the newest fix per review; per-account backfill silently gave up after 300 records, so an old review or deep reply on the 190+-site catalog often wasn't indexed at all; and editing an already-bugged review bumped its mutable ratedAt to "now", silently un-earning every fix it had already qualified for. All three are fixed: the reply (and ✅ badge) now shows on any predating review regardless of the bugged flag, lists every matching fix, backfill walks every page, and matching compares against a frozen createdAt instead of ratedAt. Merged into one record 2026-08-30 — the original three read as repetitive bot commentary stacked on a single review.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: "you added way too many comments to that page, looks bad": rendering one bot reply bubble per bugfixes.json entry meant a review of rateyourbuild that predated several rounds of self-fixes (this site keeps fixing itself) accumulated one near-identical "found the real bug" bubble per round. Merged three of the most repetitive existing entries into one, and — the durable half — the reply now always collapses into a single bubble per review no matter how many fixes match, listing them compactly instead of stacking a new comment per fix. Bugfixes.json can keep growing without the thread growing with it.
